title: GPT-6 Astra Proves Ben Green’s Problem 64 (Odd Prime-Factor Parity of p − 2) in Lean 4
whyItMatters: GPT-6 Astra produced an 83-page proof and dual-kernel Palomar-verified Lean 4 formalization showing infinitely many primes p have p − 2 with an odd number of prime factors—a weak parity cousin of Twin Primes.
summary: Registered on the Palomar Lean registry on November 13, 2026 (PALOMAR-2026-11-13-000010), GPT-6 Astra operating in a repository run by Igor Inozemtsev produced an 83-page analytic proof and complete Mathlib-only Lean 4 formalization solving Problem 64 from Ben Green’s famous list of 100 Open Problems: proving that infinitely many primes p satisfy that Ω(p − 2) is odd, where Ω counts prime factors with multiplicity. As Green notes, the problem is a weak parity form of the Twin Prime Conjecture (which asks for Ω(p − 2) = 1 infinitely often). Drawing on an October 2026 manuscript by Jizhou Guo and adapting OpenAI’s analytic number theory infrastructure, the proof constructs a nonnegative weight supported on odd prime-factor parity and applies correlation estimates with a weighted sieve, passing Comparator and both independent kernels (nanoda and con-ron).
technicalHighlights: Unconditional Mathlib-only Lean 4 proof of Problem 64 from Ben Green’s 100 Open Problems with zero extra hypotheses.
Constructs a nonnegative weight supported on odd prime-factor parity combined with correlation estimates and a weighted sieve over shifted primes u + 2.
Passed Palomar Comparator plus both independent kernels (nanoda and con-ron) against the exact FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/64.lean statement.
caveats: Builds on and adapts analytic number theory ideas from an October 2026 manuscript by Jizhou Guo and OpenAI’s Prime Predecessors library; human journal peer review is pending.
